UDC 615-472-4: 616-287-4 — 089'873-72 IS I 9564-1980 




Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 1 998 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

FORCEPS, STAPEDECTOMY, SERRATED, SMOOTH 

AND Mc GEE WIRE CLOSING JAWS 



1. Scope — Covers the dimensional and other requirements for serrated jaw, smooth jaw and Mc 
Gee wire closing jaw stapedectomy forceps used in ENT microsurgery. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1 and 1A. 

2.1 The tolerance on various dimensions shall be permitted as given below: 

± 005 mm on dimensions up to 5 mm, and 

± 0'1 mm on dimensions above 5 mm and up to 10 mm. 

2.2 Joint — As specified in 6 of Section 2 of IS: 3642-1978 'General requirements for surgical 
instruments ( first revision ) \ The joint shall be riveted. 

2.3 Finger Loops— Finger loops shall conform to size 1 of Section 5 of IS : 3642-1978. 

3. Material — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 30CM3 of IS : 6603-1972 'Specification for 
stainless steel bars and flats'. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The surfaces of the forceps shall be free from burrs, pits, cracks and other surface defects. 

4.2 All edges shall be smoothly rounded and shall not be sharp anywhere. Edges of working end 
shall be free from feather, nicks, etc, when viewed under a magnification of 10 x. 

4.3 The arms shall move freely and easily at the joint and there shall be no side play at the joint. 

4.4 When the forceps are closed the serrations shall engage accurately over the entire length. 

4.5 The serrations where specified shall be clean and well defined and shall conform to pitch 
0*3 mm specified in IS : 3642-1978. 

4.6^The forceps shall be matt finished and passivated. 

4.7 The maximum opening of the upper jaw shall correspond to the maximum opening of the finger 
loops, that is, when the finger loops are open to their maximum position the jaws shall not move 
further. 

4.8 The forceps shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 450 to 550 HV. 

5. Tests 

5.1 The forceps shall pass the tests for: ( a ) engagement of tips, ( b ) engagement of jaws, and 
( c ) uniformity of serrations prescribed in IS : 3642-1978. 

5.2 The forceps shall be tested by picking up at the tip fine hair or bits of threads and fibres strewn 
on a polished surface, for example, a glass plate. 

5.3 Corrosion Resistance — The instrument shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test as specified 
in IS : 7531-1975 ' Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel 
surgical instruments'. 



Adopted 24 July 1980

IS: 9564-1980 

6. Marking — The instrument shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials, or recognized 
trade-mark. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — The instrument shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene 
bag avoiding contact with one another. They may also be packed as agreed to between the pur- 
chaser and the supplier.
